scope: WP04 independent holdout signed protocol and operator-pinned dataset identity
WP04 inert Host SDK, Cordis Fiber-owned execution and fail-closed recovery
WP04 private evidence persistence boundary and real local subprocess transport
implemented: The published ./benchmark/holdout surface is an inert Host SDK. Importing it does not mount a Cordis plugin, open stores, spawn an authority or register model tools.
runIndependentHoldoutInContext registers the journal, evidence store, authority and delegate session, cancellation and bounded cleanup as an effect owned by the caller's current Cordis Fiber.

The operator pins an exact dataset id, version and digest plus an Ed25519 authority public key. Signed manifest, input, verdict and finish envelopes bind the public commitments, exact plan and cell identities, output digest and ordered verdict chain.
The Host validates frozen variant versions, per-cell budget, Host-reported metrics, execution evidence and quiescence. The authority does not supply resource accounting.

The benchmark journal, evidence objects and reports persist commitments, signed manifest/verdict/finish envelopes, Host metrics and evidence digests, but not the signed input envelope, raw input or raw output. Host-held input and output byte arrays are zeroed after settlement on a best-effort basis.

A complete journal plus completion marker is recursively reverified without opening the provider or delegate. Unknown results are terminal; completed prefixes, unresolved intents, missing finish markers and identity drift fail closed without selective replay.

The provider transport uses one in-flight NDJSON request, a fixed child cwd of /, a complete operator-supplied environment instead of inherited Host environment, bounded frames and stderr, request deadlines and bounded TERM-to-KILL shutdown.

The Linux evidence store pins a private 0700 evidence directory descriptor, publishes canonical 0600 content-addressed files, rejects unsafe ancestors, links and replacement, and recursively verifies the manifest, verdict and finish chain on read.

Arbitrary Host provider startup, requests and close now have a validated providerTimeoutMs. Abort or timeout fences late startup to one bounded close with no further request/store access. POSIX subprocess shutdown requires both leader closure and same-process-group disappearance; remaining descendants receive TERM then KILL, with unconfirmed cleanup rejected.

limitations: The subprocess integration uses a synthetic authority child owned by the same OS UID. It does not prove an independent UID, account, machine, trust domain or production deployment boundary.
No real-model benchmark/RSI execution, independently administered holdout dataset or live benefit comparison was run in this slice. TraeX was used only for code review.

Ed25519 signatures and content digests authenticate current envelopes but do not prove that the dataset and oracle were frozen before candidate generation. There is no external append-only transparency or timestamp anchor.
Metrics are measured or asserted by the trusted Host adapter and checked by the runner; there is no independent external resource meter.
The provider executable is validated as an absolute canonical pathname but is not fd- or inode-bound across validation and spawn, so pathname replacement is outside the guarantee.
An acceptance digest is a content commitment, not encryption. It does not keep low-entropy acceptance material secret.

On the last cell, the signed finish evidence and completion marker are published before the SQLite cell result is committed. A crash in that window leaves a running intent; after independently confirming the old execution is stopped, an operator must interrupt it to unknown rather than promote the marker to success.
The evidence store is Linux-only and depends on /proc/self/fd directory anchoring plus owner-only path and file permissions. It does not provide an equivalent non-Linux evidence-store guarantee.
The SDK and benchmark report never authorize promotion; promotionAuthorized remains false.
Best-effort zeroing and SDK-level non-persistence do not prevent an authority, delegate, model provider or same-UID process from retaining private input or raw output elsewhere.

Plain POSIX process-group cleanup does not contain descendants that leave the group and cannot rule out numeric PID/PGID reuse causing a signal to reach a different group. It is not race-free OS process identity or a strong containment boundary. Windows manages the direct child and owned stdio; unresolved inherited streams cause bounded termination-unconfirmed rather than success.
